root_cause.text: The vulnerability is caused by btrfs_create_new_inode() performing inode creation and tree modifications before checking whether the parent directory’s leaf has enough space to accommodate a new name in a hash-collision-heavy scenario, so when btrfs_add_link() later fails with -EOVERFLOW the transaction is aborted, forcing the filesystem read-only.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early call to btrfs_check_dir_item_collision() in btrfs_create_new_inode() (before any tree updates) for non-orphan, non-subvol creations, with the commit message stating: “Fix this by checking for hash collision, and if the adding a new name is possible, early in btrfs_create_new_inode() before we do any tree updates, so that we don’t need to abort the transaction if we cannot add the new name due to the leaf size limit.” The CVE description and reproducer confirm that creating many files with colliding hashes eventually triggers a transaction abort and forced readonly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add early check for directory item collision to prevent transaction abort when creating new inodes.
intent_record.what: Added a check at the beginning of btrfs_create_new_inode() to call btrfs_check_dir_item_collision() for non-orphan, non-subvol inode creations, returning an error if the check fails.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that before proceeding with inode creation, the function verifies that adding the directory entry will not cause a dir item overflow due to hash collisions, preventing a potential transaction abort.
